paper: Faisal, Fabrizio, Anastasopoulos. 'DialectBench: An NLP Benchmark for Dialects, Varieties, and Closely-Related Languages.' ACL 2024. https://aclanthology.org/2024.acl-long.777/
repo_own_license: The DialectBench repository's own code (download_data.sh, all_commands.sh, scripts/*.py, etc.) is Apache License 2.0 -- verified directly from the LICENSE file at the repo root of a real `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/ffaisal93/DialectBench.git`. This license covers DialectBench's OWN scripts only; it says nothing about the data those scripts pull, which is why this manifest carries a separate, independently-verified license per sub-source below rather than one blanket license for the whole aggregator.
aggregator_structure_as_found: DialectBench aggregates 10 NLP tasks (dependency parsing, POS tagging, NER, topic classification, NLI, sentiment analysis, dialect identification, reading comprehension/QA, machine translation) across 281 language varieties, pulled from many independently-licensed upstream sources via `download_data.sh` and `scripts/*/process_dataset.py`. Two distinct fetch mechanisms exist in the aggregator's own scripts: (1) most tasks (sib-200, sdqa-gold, ner, pos_tagging, parsing, sentiment_analysis, dialect_identification, reading_comprehension, machine_translation_turkish) are pre-bundled zip files hosted on the maintainer's personal GMU SharePoint/OneDrive share links, each bundling MANY upstream sub-datasets together with no single consolidated license statement; (2) two tasks (`sentiment_analysis_raw`, `dialect_identification_raw`) instead `git clone` a list of small, individually-named upstream GitHub repositories directly and run scripts/process_dataset.py to reshape each into train/test CSVs -- this is the mechanism this pocket actually ran and adapted, because each of its sub-sources is independently inspectable and independently licensed, which is exactly what the per-sub-source verification this pocket requires depends on.
fetch_method: Real `git clone --depth 1` of the DialectBench repository itself (to read download_data.sh and process_dataset.py verbatim), followed by real `git clone --depth 1` of each individual upstream sub-source repository named inside download_data.sh's `sentiment_analysis_raw` and `dialect_identification_raw` sections. Every LICENSE/LICENSE.md file below was read directly from its own cloned repository, not assumed from the pocket description or from memory. AJGT.xlsx was converted to CSV locally with openpyxl (columns kept: ID, Feed, Sentiment) mirroring exactly what DialectBench's own `process_ajgt()` function in scripts/process_dataset.py does, so the shape matches the aggregator's own intended use of the file.
coverage: This pocket stages 4 of DialectBench's smaller, individually-licensed sub-sources (all reached via the aggregator's own git-clone-based `sentiment_analysis_raw` / `dialect_identification_raw` fetch path) -- a small slice of the benchmark's full 281-variety / 10-task scope. Within each staged sub-source, coverage varies and is stated per-entry below: two (Greek dialect classifier, AJGT) are staged in full because the whole upstream dataset is itself small (hundreds to ~1,800 rows); two (TUNIZI, TSAC) are staged as bounded, label-stratified proportional samples (roughly 2% and 10-15% respectively) of much larger upstream files, explicitly NOT the full corpus. Nothing from the SharePoint-hosted task bundles (the other 8-9 DialectBench tasks) is staged at all -- see `sharepoint_bundles_not_attempted` below.

sub_sources.coverage: TUNIZI ships two files, both `sentence;label` format. TUNIZI_V1.txt (9,210 lines, binary label in {-1,1}: 4,372 negative / 4,838 positive) is staged in FULL -- it is the smaller of the two files and its label balance is already near-even, so no sampling was needed. TUNIZI_V2.txt (100,000 lines, three-way label in {-1,0,1}) is staged as a bounded SAMPLE of 1,999 rows (~2% of the full file) -- NOT the full corpus. The sample was drawn proportionally per label class (label counts in the full file: -1 -> 43,767; 0 -> 3,522; 1 -> 52,711) with a fixed random seed (Python `random.seed(42)`), so the sample's label balance matches the source file's true label balance rather than reflecting the file's own on-disk ordering (the raw file is sorted by label, so a naive head/tail slice would have been all-one-class; this was checked before sampling, not assumed).

license_verification.method: Real `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/fbougares/TSAC.git`, then LICENSE and README.md read directly from the cloned repository.
license_verification.found: LICENSE file at repo root: full verbatim text of the GNU Lesser General Public License, Version 3, 29 June 2007. No separate data-specific license statement exists anywhere in the repo; the README only credits the introducing WANLP 2017 paper and asks users citing the corpus to cite that paper.
license_verification.caveat_disclosed: LGPL-3.0 is a copyleft SOFTWARE license, and this repository contains a plain-text data corpus with no code -- the repo owner appears to have applied GitHub's own generic license picker to a data repo, which is common but imprecise. Treated here as an open, OSI-approved license (permissive to use/copy/redistribute, with a copyleft condition on derivative works) rather than as 'all rights reserved,' but the mismatch between a software license and a text corpus is disclosed rather than silently smoothed over. Not treated as 'clearly unrestricted public-domain-equivalent' the way the MIT/AFL sub-sources above are.
license_verification.result: Open per an explicit, verifiable license statement -- staged as a bounded, clearly-tagged SAMPLE (not staged generously) specifically because of the copyleft-on-data ambiguity just disclosed, per this repo's rule 2's middle case.

sub_sources.coverage: TSAC's four upstream files (train_pos.txt 7,152 lines, train_neg.txt 6,513 lines, test_pos.txt 1,700 lines, test_neg.txt 1,700 lines; total 17,065 lines) are staged as a bounded RANDOM sample (seed=42, no stratification needed since each file is already single-label): 700 of train_pos, 700 of train_neg, 300 of test_pos, 300 of test_neg -- 2,000 lines total, roughly 11.7% of the full corpus. Explicitly a sample, not the full corpus.

deliberately_not_staged.reason: Every one of these 9 tasks is fetched in download_data.sh exclusively via a personal GMU SharePoint/OneDrive 'share link' (URLs of the form gmuedu-my.sharepoint.com/:u:/g/personal/ffaisal_gmu_edu/...?download=1) rather than a stable public URL or a per-source repository. A live check (curl -I) of one such link returned HTTP 200 with `content-type: text/html` rather than a direct zip stream -- i.e. even mechanically, this is not a plain public file fetch but an ad-hoc, credential-adjacent sharing mechanism whose behavior for an unauthenticated automated client is not guaranteed. More importantly for the license question this pocket exists to answer: each of these zips BUNDLES many different upstream sub-datasets together (for example the `ner` bundle mixes WikiANN, which is CC-BY-SA via Wikipedia, with a separate Norwegian NER dataset; the `parsing`/`pos_tagging` bundles are built from many individual Universal Dependencies treebanks, most CC BY-SA 4.0 but not uniformly so; the pre-bundled `dialect_identification` zip includes MADAR, which itself requires a separate license agreement/registration with the Linguistic Data Consortium-adjacent MADAR release process) -- there is no single license statement covering the zip as a whole, and verifying every sub-dataset packed inside each zip was out of scope for a small, bounded pocket. Per the pocket's explicit instruction ('flag, don't attempt to work around'), these are named here and none of their content is staged, sampled, or guessed at.
